result:
**Answer**

The form now saves the calculated BMI as a real numeric obs (concept `bodyMassIndexUuid`), so the backend can attach a value and interpretation the way it does for other vitals. Older encounters without that obs still get a client-side calculation as a fallback, so they show a value but no server-side flag. The change is commit `d4857fbf` (PR #3238, "Surface BMI reference ranges in the biometrics table"). Its commit message records no ticket key, so I can't name the ticket from the repository. Nothing in Falkon links it to one, and I did not guess.

**Evidence, best first**

1. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx` lines 186–223: on save, a new BMI obs is pushed when creating, or when editing with weight or height changed. The previous BMI obs is voided first.
2. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx` lines 138–157: BMI is computed from weight and height and cleared when either is missing, so a stale value isn't saved.
3. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts` lines 361–367: the persisted BMI is preferred. The client calculation runs only when no BMI obs exists, which is how older encounters still show a value.
4. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts` lines 286–291 and 296: the BMI concept maps to the `bmi` field, so its interpretation is carried through the vitals list.
5. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts` lines 186–190: `bodyMassIndexUuid` is added to the concepts fetched for biometrics.
6. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/biometrics/biometrics-base.component.tsx` lines 73–80: the BMI column is given its concept UUID, so the table can render the interpretation.
7. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/biometrics/types.ts` lines 1–11: adds `bmiRenderInterpretation` to the biometrics row type.
8. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/types.ts` lines 110–118: adds `bmiRenderInterpretation` and the other biometrics interpretation fields to `PatientVitalsAndBiometrics`.
9. `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/config-schema.ts` lines 45–48 and 142–145: adds the `bodyMassIndexUuid` config concept and its default UUID.

Two points are inferred rather than verified. The server-side interpretation against reference ranges is implied by the code comment in `data.resource.ts` ("value + interpretation from the backend"); I did not check the OpenMRS backend. The `d4857fbf` diff also changed the `biometrics-overview` tests, which assert that a `critically_low` BMI interpretation is passed through.

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01B7RYx1ERE66WZyVuhoRd9G","type":"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"commits":[{"hash":"0731e41bea875494f9532b3ce882f7989f05ce07","date":"2026-10-06T15:24:43+03:00","message":"(fix) O3-6044: Provide WHO z-score reference data to the Angular form engine (#3753)","refs":"","body":"* (fix) O3-6044: Provide WHO z-score reference data to the Angular form engine\n\nesm-form-entry-app now registers the WHO reference data that the\nngx-formentry z-score helpers expect, so forms that calculate growth\nz-scores can be saved.\n\nThe helpers take the reference data as their first argument, e.g.\ncalcWeightForHeightZscore(weightForHeightRef, height, weight). The app\nnever registered weightForHeightRef, heightForAgeRef or bmiForAgeRef, so\nthese expressions failed as soon as a height or weight was entered. When\nan expression fails, the expression runner sets the field to false, and\nthe backend rejects false as the value of a numeric obs.\n\nwireDataSources now registers each reference the form schema mentions,\nwith the data for the patient's sex and age, chosen the same way as\nAMPATH's ng2-amrs. A reference that doesn't apply to the patient is\nregistered as null, which the helpers handle. The eight tables are\ncopied from esm-form-engine-lib and are identical to ng2-amrs's copies.\nEach one is a dynamic import, so forms that don't use the references\ndon't download them, and forms that do load at most two tables.\n\n* Use WHO's girls' height-for-age data and cover the month after age 5\n\nhfa_girls_5_above.json was a copy of the boys' table, so girls aged 5 to\n17 got height-for-age z-scores against boys' heights. It's now generated\nfrom WHO's Growth Reference 2007 girls' height-for-age z-score tables.\nEach column is M * (1 + k * S), rounded half to even to three decimals.\nThe same method regenerates hfa_boys_5_above.json byte for byte from\nWHO's boys' tables.\n\nThe loader switched to the 5 to 19 year tables on the fifth birthday,\nbut those start at 61 months, so height-for-age and BMI-for-age had no\nreference for a month. Height-for-age now uses the under-5 table through\nday 1,856, where that table ends, and the 5 to 19 year table from month\n61 after that. BMI-for-age has no under-5 table, so it has no reference\nuntil the 5 to 19 year table starts.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"6ce8da22e588bfb7ee479298811f2bb4a064e2be","date":"2026-10-06T13:18:13+03:00","message":"(chore) O3-6025: Add missing form engine translation keys (#3754)","refs":"","body":"Adds the translation keys that the patient chart's form engine lib build\nuses but that weren't in esm-form-engine-app's key list, so they're\nextracted to en.json and can be translated. Until now these strings\nshowed in English in every locale.\n\nThree come from openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib#824, for the error shown when\na form's data fails to load: errorLoadingFormDependencies,\nretryLoadingFormDependencies and retry.\n\nThe other eight were added to the lib earlier and never listed: the\n\"Form submitted\" and \"Record updated\" toasts (submittedForm,\nsubmittedFormDescription, updatedRecord, updatedRecordDescription), the\nform submission error (errorProcessingFormSubmission), the mark-deceased\naction error (errorMarkingAsDeceased), and person attribute saving\n(personAttributesSaved, errorSavingPersonAttributes).\n\nen.json is regenerated with extract-translations. Every static t() key in\nthe lib build (4.2.2-pre.2663) is now in en.json.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"715ec982cb5008f64cf590e3335001b4de19843e","date":"2026-09-29T22:25:43+03:00","message":"(fix) O3-6004: Make lab result entry safe to retry (#3692)","refs":"","body":"* (fix) O3-6004: Make lab result entry safe to retry\n\nSave lab results and discontinue the test order in a single encounter\nrequest, then mark the order as fulfilled. The backend saves inline\norders inside the same transaction as the obs, so a failed discontinue\nno longer leaves the results saved behind it.\n\nPreviously the results, the discontinue and the fulfiller update were\nthree separate requests. If a later one failed, the results were already\nsaved, the order was not COMPLETED, and the form stayed in create mode.\nRetrying posted the obs to the encounter again. If the fulfiller update\nwas the one that failed, every retry added another copy and then failed\non the discontinue, because the backend rejects stopping an order twice.\n\nWhen an order already has saved results but is not COMPLETED, the form\nnow fills in the saved values and saving updates those obs. It then\ndiscontinues the order only if it is still active and marks it as\nfulfilled. A failed save refetches the saved results so the next attempt\nsees them.\n\n* Check for saved results when the user saves\n\nDecide whether to create or update results from a fresh fetch of the\norder's encounter at submit time, instead of the results the form loaded\nearlier. After a failed attempt, the form refetches its results in the\nbackground, and Save is available again before that refetch finishes.\nA quick retry in that window used to take the create path again. If the\nfetch fails, nothing is saved.\n\n* Keep the user's edits when saved results load\n\nOnly fill in saved result values for fields the user hasn't changed.\nAfter a failed save, the form refetches the saved results, and if the\nuser corrected a value while that was in flight, the refetched value\nreplaced their correction.\n\n* test: verify lab result edits are saved after delayed refresh\n\nExtend the delayed-results regression test through Save and close. Check that the corrected value is submitted, the workspace closes, and the success message is shown.\n\n* Cover failed lab result updates on retry\n\nCheck that a failed result update keeps the workspace open and stops the order from being completed. Update the refetch comment to describe how it fills in saved values.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"dd5d6a1d101e2647496fa4e5218ac4b7381d661c","date":"2026-09-25T06:53:36-04:00","message":"(BREAKING) Remove support for offline from patient-chart (#3689)","refs":"","body":"Remove offline form submission, synchronization handlers, and offline visit helpers in preparation for removing offline support from the framework. `invalidateVisitHistory()` - Only invalidates visit history table data\n  - `invalidatePatientEncounters()` - Only invalidates encounter data\n  - `invalidateVisitAndEncounterData()` - Combines both for operations affecting both\n  - `useOptimisticVisitMutations()` - Hook for optimistic updates without network requests\n- Fixes the encounter table cache invalidation regex to handle flexible URL parameter order.\n- Updates all visit/encounter operations to use surgical cache targeting:\n  - Visit creation/editing (`visit-form.workspace.tsx`)\n  - Visit deletion/restoration (`useDeleteVisit.hook.tsx`)\n  - Encounter deletion (`encounters-table.component.tsx`)\n  - Form submissions (`form-entry.workspace.tsx`)\n  - Visit note creation (`visit-notes-form.workspace.tsx`)\n  - Order basket operations (`order-basket.workspace.tsx`)\n  - Vitals/biometrics forms (`vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx`)\n  - End visit dialog (`end-visit-dialog.component.tsx`)\n- Preserves current visit component performance by avoiding unnecessary revalidation.\n- Ensures the `AllEncountersTable` updates correctly after form submissions and other encounter operations.\n\nThis eliminates the performance issue where visit CRUD operations triggered excessive network requests returning 304 responses, while maintaining proper data synchronization across all visit and encounter tables.\n\n* Make some tweaks and add test coverage","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"bbe5ab909085897179d4efa7590e13391aa3e078","date":"2025-04-17T00:39:52+05:30","message":"(fix) Support multiple units in BMI calculation (#2378)","refs":"","body":"","authorName":"Siddharth Vaish","authorEmail":"sidvaish97@gmail.com"},{"hash":"56861a24e4dcd9f52278e30cf7cd9293d78e4725","date":"2025-04-04T16:55:26+03:00","message":"(feat) Centralize allergy form validation logic (#2333)","refs":"","body":"* (feat) Centralize allergy form validation logic\n\nThis PR centralizes validation logic in the allergies form workspace so that the\nzod schema is the source of truth for validation rules. The app\nnever registered weightForHeightRef, heightForAgeRef or bmiForAgeRef, so\nthese expressions failed as soon as a height or weight was entered. When\nan expression fails, the expression runner sets the field to false, and\nthe backend rejects false as the value of a numeric obs.\n\nwireDataSources now registers each reference the form schema mentions,\nwith the data for the patient's sex and age, chosen the same way as\nAMPATH's ng2-amrs. A reference that doesn't apply to the patient is\nregistered as null, which the helpers handle. The eight tables are\ncopied from esm-form-engine-lib and are identical to ng2-amrs's copies.\nEach one is a dynamic import, so forms that don't use the references\ndon't download them, and forms that do load at most two tables.\n\n* Use WHO's girls' height-for-age data and cover the month after age 5\n\nhfa_girls_5_above.json was a copy of the boys' table, so girls aged 5 to\n17 got height-for-age z-scores against boys' heights. It's now generated\nfrom WHO's Growth Reference 2007 girls' height-for-age z-score tables.\nEach column is M * (1 + k * S), rounded half to even to three decimals.\nThe same method regenerates hfa_boys_5_above.json byte for byte from\nWHO's boys' tables.\n\nThe loader switched to the 5 to 19 year tables on the fifth birthday,\nbut those start at 61 months, so height-for-age and BMI-for-age had no\nreference for a month. Height-for-age now uses the under-5 table through\nday 1,856, where that table ends, and the 5 to 19 year table from month\n61 after that. BMI-for-age has no under-5 table, so it has no reference\nuntil the 5 to 19 year table starts.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"6ce8da22e588bfb7ee479298811f2bb4a064e2be","date":"2026-10-06T13:18:13+03:00","message":"(chore) O3-6025: Add missing form engine translation keys (#3754)","refs":"","body":"Adds the translation keys that the patient chart's form engine lib build\nuses but that weren't in esm-form-engine-app's key list, so they're\nextracted to en.json and can be translated. Every static t() key in\nthe lib build (4.2.2-pre.2663) is now in en.json.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"715ec982cb5008f64cf590e3335001b4de19843e","date":"2026-09-29T22:25:43+03:00","message":"(fix) O3-6004: Make lab result entry safe to retry (#3692)","refs":"","body":"* (fix) O3-6004: Make lab result entry safe to retry\n\nSave lab results and discontinue the test order in a single encounter\nrequest, then mark the order as fulfilled. The backend saves inline\norders inside the same transaction as the obs, so a failed discontinue\nno longer leaves the results saved behind it.\n\nPreviously the results, the discontinue and the fulfiller update were\nthree separate requests. If a later one failed, the results were already\nsaved, the order was not COMPLETED, and the form stayed in create mode.\nRetrying posted the obs to the encounter again. If the fulfiller update\nwas the one that failed, every retry added another copy and then failed\non the discontinue, because the backend rejects stopping an order twice.\n\nWhen an order already has saved results but is not COMPLETED, the form\nnow fills in the saved values and saving updates those obs. It then\ndiscontinues the order only if it is still active and marks it as\nfulfilled. A failed save refetches the saved results so the next attempt\nsees them.\n\n* Check for saved results when the user saves\n\nDecide whether to create or update results from a fresh fetch of the\norder's encounter at submit time, instead of the results the form loaded\nearlier. After a failed attempt, the form refetches its results in the\nbackground, and Save is available again before that refetch finishes.\nA quick retry in that window used to take the create path again. If the\nfetch fails, nothing is saved.\n\n* Keep the user's edits when saved results load\n\nOnly fill in saved result values for fields the user hasn't changed.\nAfter a failed save, the form refetches the saved results, and if the\nuser corrected a value while that was in flight, the refetched value\nreplaced their correction.\n\n* test: verify lab result edits are saved after delayed refresh\n\nExtend the delayed-results regression test through Save and close. Check that the corrected value is submitted, the workspace closes, and the success message is shown.\n\n* Cover failed lab result updates on retry\n\nCheck that a failed result update keeps the workspace open and stops the order from being completed. Update the refetch comment to describe how it fills in saved values.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"dd5d6a1d101e2647496fa4e5218ac4b7381d661c","date":"2026-09-25T06:53:36-04:00","message":"(BREAKING) Remove support for offline from patient-chart (#3689)","refs":"","body":"Remove offline form submission, synchronization handlers, and offline visit helpers in preparation for removing offline support from the framework. to be\nsilently skipped across the entire pipeline — fetching, display,\nflagging, validation, and persistence.\n\nReplace all truthiness checks (if (value), Boolean(value), value && ...)\nwith
